requirements.text: Open https://quotes.toscrape.com/search.aspx, failing with a step-naming error if it cannot be reached or is not the search form.
Choose the author "Albert Einstein" and let the postback reload complete, so the tag is chosen from the reloaded, author-specific tag list (no race with the old document).
Choose the tag "inspirational"; if it is not offered, fail naming the step and what was offered.

Press Search and wait until the results document (the postback to /filter.aspx) has finished loading before reading it; a wait keyed to the wrong URL or to the first result element only does not meet this.
Return every quote shown as typed objects with text, author and tag, read with locators that match the results page (.quote with .content, .author, .tag).
When no quote matches, return an empty list and say so, while a broken, changed or too-slow results page fails instead of being read as no match.
When the page does not behave as described, fail with an error that names the step and what was seen.
Close everything the program opened (browser/connection, Run or context, page) on every path, including failures.

programs.notes: Correct flow: waits for the inspirational option after the author postback, then clicks Search and waits for networkidle before reading .content/.author. But no .quote within 3 s is turned into an empty list with no Page check or heading check, so an error page or changed layout reads as 'no match'.

It wraps the Search click in page.expect_response(_is_search_response), which only matches URLs ending in /search.aspx. Search posts to /filter.aspx, so that wait hits deadline_exceeded and the program raises FormStepError instead of returning quotes. An empty result would also not be told apart from a broken page.

Waits for the exact tag option after the author postback, arms wait_for_response("**/filter.aspx").during(click), waits for the load, reads with the right selectors, and closes the page, Run and connection on every path. A count of 0 returns an empty list with no status, Page or heading check, so a broken results page reads as no match.

Author, tag and Search steps are sound and context/browser close in finally. After the click it reads as soon as the first div.quote is attached, without a load wait. If no quote appears within 10 s it returns [], so a slow site or changed layout silently reads as no match.

Same shape as the Python sonnet leader: it reads once the first .quote is visible, without waiting for the results document to load. A TimeoutError on that wait becomes an empty list, so a slow or changed results page is reported as no match.

The Search step waits for a response matching /\/search\.aspx/, but Search posts to /filter.aspx, so it times out. Even past that, it reads span.text, which the results page does not have (its text is .content), so textContent hits its deadline.

The reload marker handles the author postback well. But the results are read as soon as a .quote exists, not after load, and each quote's text comes from .text, which the results page does not have (.content), so text_content fails and the program raises.

Search is wrapped in wait_for_response with a predicate for search.aspx, which never matches the /filter.aspx postback, so the step fails with deadline_exceeded. It also reads span.text and small.author, which do not match the results page's .content/.author spans.

expect_navigation around both postbacks is sound, and the context and browser are closed. But it reads span.text and small.author, which the filter.aspx results do not have, so inner_text times out and the program raises SearchStepError instead of returning the quote.

Navigation waits and cleanup are sound, but it reads .text, which the results page lacks (.content). allTextContents returns [] against 1 quote block, so it throws the 'quote blocks but 0 quote texts' StepError instead of returning the quote.
